subject: POC Kickoff Recap & Next Steps — Acme Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC Kickoff Recap & Next Steps — Acme Retail

Hi Sarah / Kevin —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps for the 6-week pilot (POC):

Scope (what we agreed):
- Goal: Improve search-to-conversion by improving product recommendation relevance and reducing query handling latency for personalized recommendations.
- Core integration points: Real-time recommendation API (server-side), batch embedding refresh for nightly catalog updates, and a small feedback loop for clicks.
- Included models: Redwood-recommended 7B quantized variant for inference + fallback smaller model for noisy queries.

Success metrics / acceptance criteria:
- Primary: +8–12% uplift in add-to-cart rate on A/B traffic within 4 weeks of model freeze.
- Secondary: 99th % latency under 300ms for single-request inference (p95 < 120ms), and cost target <$0.005 per evaluated request after batching.

Owners & roles:
- Acme: Sarah Jensen (Product Owner), Kevin Lee (Engineering lead)
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (AE, program owner), Dylan Brooks (Solutions Engineer, infra & access), Lauren Bishop (Customer Success)

Timeline (high-level):
- Week 0 (this week): Access & infra setup; prompt-set and eval templates shared (action: Redwood)
- Week 1: Baseline data ingest + sample runs on dev traffic; collect eval metrics (action: Acme + Redwood)
- Weeks 2–3: Iterate on prompts/temperature and quantization settings; finalize model variant (action: joint)
- Weeks 4–6: Ramp to A/B experiment; measure results and prepare rollup deck (action: joint)

Access / setup steps (what Dylan will need):
1) Create a service account with API key for dev environment (scoped to recommendation endpoints).
2) Provide a sample of catalog JSON (5–10k SKUs) and representative user history (anonymized).
3) IP allowlist range for dev and staging (we will provide Redwood egress IPs) or SAML SSO connection for private projects.
4) Grant S3/GCS read access for nightly catalog artifact (optional for batch refresh).

Attachments shared with this message: 20260225-acme-poc-scope.xlsx (scope & acceptance), acme-prompt-set-v1.json (starter prompts), redwood-poc-access-guide.pdf (technical steps).

Next steps (owners):
- Dylan: Share precise IP ranges + service-account template by Fri 2026-02-27 (ACTION: Dylan)
- Sarah: Share sample catalog + anonymized user-history by Mon 2026-03-02 (ACTION: Sarah)
- Marissa: Create HubSpot deal and share calendar invites for weekly syncs (ACTION: Marissa)

If anything above is incorrect or missing, call it out and I will update. Thanks — excited to get started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Hi Kevin / Sarah —

Quick technical note from my side on access and dev spin-up:

Access options (pick one):
- Option A (fastest): Issue a Redwood service account API key scoped to the dev recommendation endpoint. We'll provide a key template and rotation guidance. No VPN required.
- Option B (preferred for security teams): SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning into the Redwood Private control plane (requires you to approve our metadata and usually takes 2–3 business days).
- Option C: IP allowlist to a dedicated dev egress pool (we'll share ranges).

Needed from Acme today to unblock dev:
1) A single sample catalog file (CSV or JSON, 5–10k SKUs) — path or upload to the Drive link you already have.
2) A small anonymized user-history sample (top 10k events) or a synthetic substitute if you need more time.
3) If you choose Option C, confirm the CIDR(es) to allow and we'll add to the dev ACL.

Where to find prompts/evals: I uploaded the starter prompt set to the shared Drive folder (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3Cacme-poc — file acme-prompt-set-v1.json). If you want to add business-specific templates, drop them in /prompts/ and ping me.

Spin-up ETA: If we get the sample data + access chosen today, I can have a dev instance running with sample inference in 36–48 hours (target: Fri 2026-02-27).

Attaching: redwood-poc-access-guide.pdf (small PDF with the service-account template and IP ranges).

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
